newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka, Tigers trade charges on Paris killings.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka, Tigers trade charges on Paris killings.

text.p: Sri Lanka's government and Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels traded accusations again on Tuesday over the recent killings of two rebel officials in Paris.
The government issued a fresh statement hinting that Tamil Tiger rebels may have been responsible for the deaths of their own people in late October.

"There is reason to suppose that the killings may have been of a well-known pattern, whereby the LTTE disposes of its cadres who have fallen out of favour with its leadership," the foreign ministry statement said.
The statement also said that the rebels were planning to display the victims' bodies in European capitals for propaganda purposes.
"The government has learnt informally that the LTTE intends to arrange for the bodies of these terrorist cadres to be exhibited in various European capitals...," it said.
But the LTTE's Paris-based international spokesman, Lawrence Thilakar, denied both charges.
He accused Colombo of being behind the killings and said funerals for the two officials will be held in Paris on Sunday and the burials on Tuesday.

"The bodies will be made available in a public place in Paris for people to pay their last respects," he told Reuters by telephone. "We have no plans to exhibit the bodies in other European capitals."
"(The killings) were definitely the work of the Sri Lankan government," he said.

Paris police have said that LTTE treasurer Kandiah Perinpanathan, and Kandiah Gajendran, editor of the Tamil weekly newspaper Eela Murasu, were shot dead by a gunman in the predominantly immigrant La Chapelle district of northern Paris on October 26. The gunman escaped.
The LTTE is fighting for independence for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
